headline: RARE EARTH STOCKS SNAP BACK AS APEC OPENS — USAR Surges 7%, MP Materials Jumps 8%, US Antimony Rallies 7% on US-China Talks Hopes
snippet: Rare earth equities reversed sharply on the afternoon of November 18 as traders positioned ahead of Trump-Xi bilateral meetings at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with USAR climbing 7% from its morning 52-week low, MP Materials adding 8%, and United States Antimony Corp rallying 7%. The simultaneous rebound across all three names suggests the market is pricing a non-zero probability that the January 10, 2027 expiry of China's rare earth export control pause will be extended — the central rare earth agenda item at the summit.

headline: ASIA COPPER WEEK HEARS 'RECESSIONARY-LIKE DEMAND' AS PRICE CRATERS — Physical Traders Warn AI Unwind and Tariff Fears Worse Than 2015
snippet: Delegates at Asia Copper Week 2026 in Singapore heard physical traders describe current demand signals as 'recessionary-like' — the most bearish assessment the annual gathering has heard in over a decade — as LME copper simultaneously broke below key support levels on AI sector weakness and tariff uncertainty. The juxtaposition of a weakening financial market price and tightening physical ore supply was described as 'completely disconnected' by multiple participants, with Chinese smelters approaching processing capacity limits even as LME contracts fall.

headline: NEWMONT CRATERS 5.7% TO $104, FREEPORT PLUNGES 7.6% TO $51 — Zero Sell Ratings on Either Stock Despite 22-37% Drawdowns From August Peaks
snippet: Newmont Mining (NEM) dropped 5.7% to $104.89 and Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) fell 7.6% to $51.07 on November 18, pushing them 22% and 37.5% respectively below their August 2026 peaks, yet no analyst firm currently carries a Sell rating on either. Schaeffer's identifies the disconnect as a potential sentiment trap for retail investors who might interpret the lack of sell ratings as a bottom signal — when the actual story is a consensus slow to adjust to a changed macro environment.

headline: COPPER PRICE COLLAPSE IGNORES WORSENING ORE SHORTAGE — China Smelters Near Capacity Limits as LME Hits 5-Month Low
snippet: Crux Investor identifies a deepening paradox in copper: LME prices are at five-month lows driven by financial market selling, while Chinese copper smelters are running near processing capacity limits and domestic ore supply is tightening. The piece argues that financial market participants are creating a temporary price dislocation that ignores the structural supply-side argument — a thesis that history suggests eventually reasserts itself when financial conditions normalize, potentially creating significant re-rating opportunities for copper development projects.

headline: KINROSS GOLD BUCKS SECTOR SELLOFF AHEAD OF NOV 19 EX-DIVIDEND DATE — Technical Value Buyers Step In as Name Nears Multi-Month Low
snippet: Kinross Gold (K) traded higher on November 18 against a backdrop of broad gold miner selling, with Investing.com attributing the move to technical value buyers and ex-dividend positioning ahead of a November 19 record date. For investors tracking individual name divergences within the sector selloff, Kinross's ability to hold ground while NEM and FCX fell 5-7% is a relative-strength signal worth monitoring as a potential early indicator of where institutional capital may be repositioning.

headline: GOLD'S LOSING STREAK DRIVES 10 MINERS TO OVERSOLD TERRITORY — Gold Reserve and Contango Silver Fall Below RSI 30; GLD Down 13% YTD
snippet: Seeking Alpha identified 10 gold mining stocks showing oversold RSI readings as spot gold hit 52-week lows on November 18, down 13% year to date — with Gold Reserve and Contango Silver & Gold the only names currently below the RSI 30 threshold that historically defines extreme oversold conditions. For contrarian investors, the note identifies this level of technical distress as the zone where mean-reversion buying has historically generated the strongest returns, though the macro catalyst required for a reversal remains absent until the December 9 FOMC decision.

headline: SAGA METALS LOGS 109m AT 49.88% Fe2O3, 8.53% TiO2 AND 0.316% V2O5 AT RADAR — 102 of 102 Holes Return Oxide Mineralization in Saskatchewan
snippet: SAGA Metals (TSX-V: SAGA) reported a 109.1-metre intercept returning 49.88% Fe2O3, 8.53% TiO2 and 0.316% V2O5 at its Radar Critical Minerals Project in Saskatchewan, with the company confirming that all 102 logged drill holes containing oxide mineralization have been counted — a 100% hit rate across a large dataset. The continuous, bulk-tonnage style mineralization is relevant to investors because both titanium and vanadium are on Canada's critical minerals list due to EV battery and aerospace applications, and a 100% drill success rate at scale is statistically rare in early-stage programs.

headline: GLOBAL ENERGY METALS HITS 37,265 CPS URANIUM ANOMALY IN SASKATCHEWAN — Charlot-Neely Lake Peak Radioactivity Among Highest Logged in the Basin Margin
snippet: Global Energy Metals (TSX-V: GEMC) reported peak radioactivity readings of 37,265 counts-per-second at its Charlot-Neely Lake project in Saskatchewan — a reading that places the anomaly among the highest surface radioactivity results reported in the Athabasca Basin margin, where peak CPS anomalies of this magnitude have historically preceded high-grade drill discoveries. The result comes as URNM equity prices trade at year lows despite uranium spot above $91/lb, potentially flagging undervalued grassroots targets being ignored by a market focused on macro headwinds.

headline: MEGAWATT METALS ADVANCES ATHABASCA URANIUM DRILL PROGRAM — Saskatchewan Explorer Pushes Exploration Efforts Forward
snippet: Megawatt Metals announced the advancement of its uranium exploration program in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, adding to a cluster of active junior programs targeting high-grade uranium in a jurisdiction that hosts the world's highest-grade known deposits. The announcement arrives as uranium equity prices trade at significant discounts to spot — a disconnect that has historically resolved through either equity re-ratings or M&A by larger producers seeking near-term feed for contracted reactor fuel supply.

headline: 4 GOLD MINERS POSITIONED TO SURVIVE THE CURRENT SELLOFF — Analysts Identify Names With Balance Sheet and Cost-Structure Resilience
snippet: An analyst note identified four gold mining stocks with the balance sheet strength, hedging strategies and cost structures to weather a prolonged gold price correction — a timely analysis as spot gold sits at 52-week lows with no clear reversal catalyst before the December 9 FOMC decision. The piece serves as a useful framework for retail investors deciding which names to hold through the current drawdown versus which to exit, particularly relevant as the sector's most-followed large-caps (NEM, FCX) are showing sharp relative weakness and no analyst downgrade has yet followed.
